dedupe_keys.name: wind velocity vertical profile in a 50 m wind mast at sisal yucatan mexico

description: UNAM and LANRESC publish wind and turbulence statistics from a coastal mast at Sisal, Yucatán, Mexico, for wind-power assessment. The June 2020 Zenodo release supplies a CSV and detailed text dictionary, freely available under CC BY-NC 4.0. The dictionary gives coverage from 29 July 2010 to 23 May 2012, with thirty-minute averages derived from ten-hertz acquisition at 3, 6, 12.5, 25 and 51 metres. Fields include rotated velocity components, temperature, variances, covariances, friction velocity, Monin–Obukhov length, turbulent kinetic energy and a quality-control flag. These observations can calibrate wind-resource and near-surface turbulence simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this campaign. The landing page mentions the broader 2010–2014 experiment; the published file has the shorter documented period. Rotation and direction conventions require the dictionary, and failed quality checks are represented with NaN. Sensor uncertainty and record completeness were not independently checked.
